totals.rows_scoped: contract.invariants, contract.not_exposed, instructions and best_practices across the six build-layer skills assigned to this part (build-research-record, build-simplicity-budget, build-skill-authoring, build-solution-architecture, build-status-table, build-worked-example). definition_of_done, adapters and composes_with were off limits per instruction and not touched. contract.operations, contract.shapes, contract.standards, purpose and open_questions were not in scope and not touched, matching the instruction's four named row kinds.

method: Same method as 42-sourcing-2b (core/seam layer) and its precedents: for each proposed row in the four scoped kinds, ran python3 tools/kb.py show plus grep -i over kb/facts.jsonl, kb/target-facts.jsonl (including the T-t10-* items new to this ceremony), kb/reference-facts.jsonl, kb/research.jsonl (each skill's own X-<skill>-* lens where one exists; build-status-table, build-solution-architecture and build-worked-example have no research lens of their own, confirmed by grep before leaving their rows proposed) and kb/decisions.jsonl, kb/architecture.jsonl, kb/ledger.jsonl for background only. Converted to sourced only when a verbatim quote from a cited record supported the row's own specific claim, not merely its general topic: this is why several rows that already carried a background citation in their proposed form (build-research-record's invariants on version-verified-only-when-fetched and quote-is-a-paraphrase-fails, build-simplicity-budget's eighth-design-rule framing) stayed proposed rather than converting on the strength of an adjacent but non-supporting record. Two rows already carried a citation and quote that in fact supported their own specific claim outright (build-simplicity-budget's reject-not-warn invariant against the Kubernetes ResourceQuota record, and its budget-never-caps-capability not_exposed row against the progressive-disclosure API record); these converted with no new research needed, just the origin flip and the dropped 'Proposed:' marker. No row was deleted or replaced with a sibling pointer this iteration: none of the 76 proposed rows across the six skills were found to restate a sibling skill's contract beyond what an already-present one-clause pointer covers (build-skill-authoring's compose-by-name-not-by-copy row and build-simplicity-budget's per-skill-authoring-budget row were already exactly such pointers, and were left as-is). The 64 rows that stayed proposed had a concrete research query appended verbatim to their text (or instruction action field) naming what a fetched source would need to establish to convert the row; a handful of purely internal-tooling rows (this repo's own script names, field orders, or v1 scope decisions with no external literature to speak of) were marked 'Not externally researchable' instead of given a query, and two pure references/*.md progressive-disclosure navigation pointers (build-research-record step 10, build-simplicity-budget step 9) were left untouched with no added text, matching the sourcing-01/02b/02c precedent that a navigational pointer is not researchable in the same sense.
quality_note: Every candidate quote was checked against schemas/skill.schema.json's own verbatim-substring rule before conversion (validate_skills.py's identical check). Cross-skill quote reuse was checked against each edited skill's composes_with.builds_on chain plus agentic-stack: converting build-research-record's best_practices row and build-skill-authoring's best_practices row both required re-wording around the literal phrase 'already states' so the new origin=sourced rows would not trip the restate-and-extend (MECH-2) detector while still crediting F-a7-03 by name. tools/render_skill.py and tools/validate_skills.py --only <skill> were run after every skill and again together at the end: final result is 0 errors for all six skills, and the pre-existing MECH-2 warnings (0-5 per skill, all in rows this ceremony did not touch) are byte-identical in count and content to the pre-ceremony baseline, verified by running the same validator invocation before any edit and diffing the warning lines - no new warning was introduced. A full-repo python3 tools/validate_skills.py (all 102 skills) also reports 0 errors after this ceremony's edits.
